states.name: paragraph
states.gap: Larger glyphs on the same fixed 74px line advance leave less white channel between lines: line-1 descender bottom y=227 to line-2 ascender top y=261 is 34px of clear space, against B's 224→261 = 37px — an 8% narrower gap, so in a mode whose whole job is detaching one line from its neighbours, A's rows sit closer together than B's.
states.gapTheirs: The text block leans right: 72px left indent against a 35px right gutter at the longest line (line 2 ink ends x=1705 of 1740), where A's longest line ends x=1673 for a 67px right gutter that nearly matches its 72px left. A 2:1 gutter imbalance with the rag running to within 35px of the window edge, on the same viewport and the same left indent.
states.verdict: These are the same design twice, and the split comes down to where the column sits and how big the type is. B crowds the right edge — 72px of left indent and 35px of right gutter means the block visibly leans, and on the second line the rag runs almost into the window; a writer feels that as the page pulling sideways while trying to hold one line. A gives up 3px of interline clearance and about one x-height-unit of airiness (x-height 24px vs 23px, ascender 32 vs 30) to keep the block centred and the rag comfortable, which is the better trade for staring at two dimmed lines for an hour. Neither one earns anything on the actual focus behaviour: identical single dim tier, identical body ink, no caret on screen, and two undimmed sentences in both, so the dimming itself is a wash and this is decided on the column.

states.name: dark-sentence-typewriter
states.gap: B's typewriter is off centre: the caret sits at y816–889 (centre 852 of 1800 = 47.4%), 48 device px / 24 CSS px above the window's vertical midline, while A parks its caret at y864–939 (centre 901.5 = 50.1%) — dead centre. states.gapTheirs: A renders THREE dim tiers where the design has two: on the caret line, the lit sentence 'beside it.' is #CCCCCC (204), the very next sentence 'The door took both hands to open.' is #888888 (136, ~3,404 px of solid fill from x686–1736), and only from 'Outside, the wind' onward does it drop to the real dim #707070 (112). B holds a single dim (#707070) for everything outside the sentence — 204 → 112, one step, no halo.
states.verdict: A's focus mode lies to you: it lights the sentence at #CCCCCC and then gives the following sentence its own #888888 halo, so your eye finishes 'beside it.' and is immediately dragged sideways into the next clause at 3.8:1 contrast against the 2.55:1 everything else sits at — that is a gradient, not a focus, and it defeats the point of sentence scope. B's dimming is one clean step with nothing in between, so the lit sentence is genuinely the only thing on the page. B's cost is that the caret line rests 24 CSS px above centre instead of on it, which is under a third of a line and something you notice on the tenth paragraph, not the first. A also can't hold a left edge: body at x623, the h1 words at 673, the h2 words at 698 — three margins in one document, where B hangs '#' and '##' out into the gutter and keeps all prose flush at 623.
